newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down vs Sing on unwinding, follows majors.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down vs Sing on unwinding, follows majors.

text.p: The ringgit/Singapore dollar crosses were well offered in early London trading on renewed interest to unwind positions, dealers said on Thursday.
They said against the dollar, the ringgit was tracking the trend in dollar/yen and dollar/mark.
"The market is fairly quiet. There is still interest to sell ringgit against Sing," said a dealer with a U.S bank in London.
He said there was a likelihood of dollar/yen and dollar/mark turning biddish in later trading, which could cause a further decline of the ringgit.
One dealer in Singapore said there could be some selling interest in dollar/ringgit after the U.S. market opened.
Earlier, ringgit ended marginally lower in Kuala Lumpur on dollar buying by Hong Kong and Kuala Lumpur-based investors.
"There were some offers at 2.5265 level earlier, but very small deals were done," the Singapore dealer said.
Dealers said if ringgit/Singapore dollar hit 0.5540, there could be some stop-loss selling.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5265/72 a dollar against 2.5245/55 previously. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5543/47 a ringgit against 0.5547/54. - Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911)
